# Deploy Center

> Free, open-source (MIT) Mac app, Mac widgets and bash CLI that turns off Git auto-deploy on Vercel, Render and other hosts, so you stop paying for a build on every push. It shows the commits and pull requests waiting to go live and the build costs, and deploys what changed when you decide. Made for AI coding: the agent pushes as often as it likes, you deploy once; Autofix hands a failed build to a Claude Code routine that opens a fix PR; Claude in the app explains failures, writes release notes and checks if a change is safe to ship; Claude Desktop and Claude Code connect through an MCP server and a Claude Code plugin.

- Version: 0.14.0 (macOS app and `deploys` CLI).
- Hosts: Vercel and Render on by default; Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, AWS Amplify, DigitalOcean App Platform, Coolify, Fly.io, Railway, Heroku, Firebase Hosting, GitHub Pages, Koyeb, Northflank, Deno Deploy and any deploy hook opt-in (16 providers in all). Sources: GitHub and GitLab.
- Safe deploys: in the CLI only when CI is green (`--when-green`), a site check with automatic rollback, deploy windows, a risk score, and a guard that turns auto-deploy off again every 30 minutes.
- Savings: a simulator before you switch and a ledger afterwards, all marked as estimates.
- Everywhere: window, menu bar, Dock badge, Mac widgets, command palette (Cmd-K); an iPhone and iPad app with Face ID is on its way to the App Store.
- Teams: a shared deploy-center.json per repo, observer mode, and an optional two-person rule, without a server.
- Integrations: VS Code/Cursor/Windsurf extension, Raycast, GitHub Action, badges, daily summary to Slack/Discord/Telegram/ntfy, status page, pre-push hook, Docker image.
- Requirements: macOS 15 or later (app, universal); the `deploys` CLI is bash and installs on macOS, Linux, WSL and CI (`curl -fsSL https://deploycenter.app/install.sh | sh`).
- Privacy: no account, no telemetry, no server of its own. Your own logins and keys in the macOS keychain. Claude features are opt-in, use your own Anthropic key and send only masked text.
- Not affiliated with Vercel, Render, Netlify, Cloudflare, AWS, DigitalOcean, Coolify, GitHub, GitLab or Anthropic. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic.
- Topics (each has a guide below): disable Vercel auto-deploy, Render auto-deploy off, Vercel Ignored Build Step, Vercel build cost, Netlify stop builds, deploy hooks, Claude Code with Vercel, fix failed Vercel builds with AI.

## Guides

- [All guides](https://deploycenter.app/guides/)
- [Disable Vercel auto-deploy](https://deploycenter.app/guides/disable-vercel-auto-deploy/): Three ways to stop Vercel deploying on every push, and how to undo each.
- [Stop Vercel building every push](https://deploycenter.app/guides/stop-vercel-building-every-push/): Build less without turning Git off: previews, bots, monorepos, batching.
- [Vercel Ignored Build Step](https://deploycenter.app/guides/vercel-ignored-build-step/): Script examples for the ignore command, and the pitfalls that make it build anyway.
- [Turn off Render auto-deploy](https://deploycenter.app/guides/render-auto-deploy-off/): Dashboard, render.yaml autoDeployTrigger: off, and the Render API.
- [Stop Netlify builds](https://deploycenter.app/guides/netlify-stop-builds/): stop_builds versus an ignore command that only lets build hooks through.
- [Reduce Vercel costs](https://deploycenter.app/guides/reduce-vercel-costs/): A checklist: builds first, then functions, images and bandwidth.
- [Auto-fix failed builds with Claude](https://deploycenter.app/guides/auto-fix-failed-vercel-builds-with-claude/): A failed Vercel or Render build goes to a Claude Code routine, which opens a fix PR.
- [Deploy hooks for any host](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-hooks/): What a deploy hook is, where each host keeps it, calling it with curl, keeping the URL secret.
- [Vercel build minutes and the build queue](https://deploycenter.app/guides/vercel-build-minutes-and-build-queue/): How builds add up from pushes, projects and branches, and how to measure them.
- [Deploy to Vercel from GitHub Actions](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-to-vercel-from-github-actions/): A deploy hook on a label, a prebuilt deploy, or one daily deploy of what changed.
- [Skip Vercel previews for bots and agents](https://deploycenter.app/guides/skip-vercel-previews-for-bots-and-agents/): An Ignored Build Step for Dependabot, Renovate and AI agent branches.
- [Ignored Build Step or auto-deploy off](https://deploycenter.app/guides/ignored-build-step-or-auto-deploy-off/): What each skips, what still creates a deployment, and when a script is the wrong tool.
- [Stop Cloudflare Pages builds](https://deploycenter.app/guides/cloudflare-pages-stop-builds/): Turn off production and preview deployments so a push no longer uses a build.
- [Disable AWS Amplify auto-build](https://deploycenter.app/guides/aws-amplify-disable-auto-build/): One AWS CLI command per branch, and how to start a build yourself.
- [Stop DigitalOcean App Platform builds](https://deploycenter.app/guides/digitalocean-app-platform-deploy-on-push/): deploy_on_push: false on each component, and why the API needs the whole spec.
- [Coolify: Auto Deploy off](https://deploycenter.app/guides/coolify-auto-deploy-off/): No build storm on your own server: the switch, the API field, deploying by hand.
- [Roll back a Vercel or Render deploy](https://deploycenter.app/guides/roll-back-vercel-render-deployment/): Back to the last good deployment from the dashboard or the CLI, and how to check.
- [How to save build minutes on any host](https://deploycenter.app/guides/save-build-minutes/): Build minutes are builds times build time. Count your builds, cut the ones nobody needs, then shorten the rest, on Vercel, Netlify, Render or Cloudflare.
- [Your deploy queue: what is merged but not live](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-queue/): See which commits and pull requests are merged but not live, plan the next deploy, start it on purpose and watch or cancel it, with the deploys CLI.
- [Roll back automatically when a deploy breaks the site](https://deploycenter.app/guides/automatic-rollback-after-deploy/): Ask the live site after every deploy and go back to the previous deployment on a 5xx: deploys verify, its exit codes, and the countdown in the app.
- [Skip preview builds for bots on Netlify, Cloudflare and Render](https://deploycenter.app/guides/skip-preview-builds-for-bots-netlify-cloudflare-render/): Stop Dependabot, Renovate and coding-agent branches from starting preview builds on Netlify, Cloudflare Pages and Render, and keep previews for people.
- [Monorepo ignore rules: build only the app that changed](https://deploycenter.app/guides/monorepo-skip-unchanged-builds/): One push builds every project connected to a monorepo. Skip the unchanged ones on Vercel, Netlify, Render and Cloudflare Pages, and avoid the usual pitfalls.
- [Set up a deploy freeze for Friday afternoon](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-freeze-friday/): Block production deploys on Friday afternoon, on weekends and on holidays with a deploy window, and let a hotfix through with a reason that is journaled.
- [Set up a status page for your deploys](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-status-page/): Publish a static what-shipped-when page with an Atom feed and status.json from your deploy history, on any static host, without exposing commit messages.
- [Reduce build costs on Netlify, Render and Cloudflare Pages](https://deploycenter.app/guides/reduce-build-costs-netlify-render-cloudflare/): A per-host checklist to cut builds on Netlify, Render and Cloudflare Pages: stop push builds, skip what nobody needs and deploy on your schedule.
- [Deploy only when CI is green](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-only-when-ci-is-green/): Ship only commits whose checks passed: deploys deploy-changed --when-green waits for running checks, skips red ones and deploys exactly the checked commit.
- [Deploy once a day on a schedule](https://deploycenter.app/guides/scheduled-daily-deploy/): Let one scheduled job deploy what changed, once a day, only when CI is green: deploys schedule on a Mac, or a GitHub Actions workflow, and what to watch out for.
- [Check what a deploy would ship: risk, diff and secrets](https://deploycenter.app/guides/check-before-you-deploy/): Before you deploy, read the diff, the risk score and a secrets check of what is merged but not live: deploys risk, diff, notes and secrets, with the rules they use.
- [Check your setup: tools, logins and keys](https://deploycenter.app/guides/check-your-setup-deploys-doctor/): See what is missing before a deploy fails: tools, GitHub login, platform keys and how old they are, one line each with the fix, using deploys doctor and creds.
- [Deploy metrics in Grafana, without a server](https://deploycenter.app/guides/prometheus-metrics-for-deploys/): Write waiting commits, their age, failed deploys and auto-deploy state as a Prometheus text file for node_exporter and Grafana, with deploys metrics.
- [Find projects that nobody deploys](https://deploycenter.app/guides/find-projects-nobody-deploys/): List every project with no deploy for 90 days or any number you choose, so you can pause or delete what you no longer need, with the deploys idle command.
- [Find TLS certificates that run out soon](https://deploycenter.app/guides/tls-certificate-expiry-check/): Check the TLS certificate of every project's address in one command, get an exit code for a scheduler or CI, and see who is unreachable, with deploys certs.
- [A weekly digest of your deploys](https://deploycenter.app/guides/weekly-deploy-digest/): Get the last week of your deploys in one block: deploys, failures, rollbacks, the busiest day, the projects and the estimated saving, with deploys digest.
- [Deploys in a row without a failure: your streak](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploys-in-a-row-without-failure/): Count how many deploys in a row went live without a failure, per project, now and at best, and see when the last failure was, with deploys streak.
- [When do your deploys fail most often?](https://deploycenter.app/guides/which-day-do-deploys-fail/): Find out whether your deploys fail more often on a weekday or at an hour of the day, from your own history, and what to do with it, with deploys when.
- [How long do failed deploys last? Recovery time](https://deploycenter.app/guides/how-long-do-failed-deploys-last/): Measure how long a failure lasted until the next deploy of that project, per project and as a typical value, and see open outages, with deploys recovery.
- [A deploy timeline: what happened, day by day](https://deploycenter.app/guides/deploy-timeline/): Read what your deploys did in the last days: deploys, failures, rollbacks and forced starts per day, from the journal, with the deploys CLI.
- [A build gate for Claude Code agents that hang your Mac](https://deploycenter.app/guides/mac-hangs-when-agents-build-together/): A build gate: heavy commands wait for memory, swap and load to leave room. Works as a Claude Code hook.
- [Forecast this month's Vercel build bill](https://deploycenter.app/guides/forecast-your-monthly-vercel-build-bill/): deploys forecast projects the spend so far to the end of the month, per project, with a budget warning.
- [Compare production and preview variables](https://deploycenter.app/guides/env-diff-missing-variables-production-preview/): deploys env-diff compares production and preview variable names on Vercel, never values.

## Comparisons

- [All comparisons](https://deploycenter.app/compare/)
- [Stop push builds: Vercel, Netlify, Render, Cloudflare compared](https://deploycenter.app/compare/stop-push-builds-compared/): The switch that stops a push from building on Vercel, Netlify, Render and Cloudflare Pages, side by side: what it stops, what it keeps, and what to watch out for.
- [Deploy on demand: hook, CLI, Actions or Deploy Center](https://deploycenter.app/compare/ways-to-deploy-on-demand/): Four ways to ship when you decide, after push builds are off: a deploy hook, the host's own CLI or button, GitHub Actions, and Deploy Center. What each gives you.
- [Scheduled deploys: cron, GitHub Actions or deploys schedule](https://deploycenter.app/compare/scheduled-deploys-compared/): Three ways to deploy on a timetable: cron with a deploy hook, a GitHub Actions schedule, and deploys schedule. Where each runs, what it checks and when it stops.
- [Deploy status page: static file or hosted status service](https://deploycenter.app/compare/status-page-compared/): A static what-shipped-when page from Deploy Center against a hosted status service: what each shows, who runs it, what leaves your machine and what it cannot do.

## Tools and reading

- [Deploy Center + Claude Code](https://deploycenter.app/claude-code/): Let the agent push, you decide what ships.
- [Build cost calculator](https://deploycenter.app/vercel-build-cost-calculator/): What auto-deploy costs a month, and what deploying by hand would cost.
- [Vercel-Build-Kosten-Rechner (Deutsch)](https://deploycenter.app/de/vercel-build-kosten-rechner/): The calculator in German.
- [AI coding agents and your build bill](https://deploycenter.app/blog/ai-coding-agents-build-bill/): Your agent pushes 40 times. You deploy once.
- [A Friday freeze should be a setting, not a rule](https://deploycenter.app/blog/friday-freeze-is-a-setting/): A deploy freeze that depends on people remembering fails when it matters. Put it in a file, record the exceptions, keep rollbacks open and close the side doors.
- [Count your builds before you cut them](https://deploycenter.app/blog/count-your-builds-before-you-cut/): Before you change a single setting, find out where your builds come from. A formula, four commands and the order in which cutting builds pays off.
- [Previews are for people: a policy for bots and agents](https://deploycenter.app/blog/previews-are-for-people/): A preview build earns its cost when a person looks at it. A short policy: previews for pull requests people review, none for bot and agent branches.
- German versions: [Anleitungen](https://deploycenter.app/de/anleitungen/), [Vergleiche](https://deploycenter.app/de/vergleich/), [Blog](https://deploycenter.app/de/blog/).
